verdict: Disney grew revenue 2% to $23.7B and segment profit 8% to $4.6B — Experiences hit $2.5B and streaming turned solidly profitable — while a $3.3B one-off tax benefit on the Hulu deal more than doubled reported net income to $5.9B.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: vs $1.43 a year ago — flattered by a $3.3B tax benefit

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment charges
opex.note: Primarily an impairment of an equity investment.

follow100Note: Of the $25.13 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, about $2.88 belongs to noncontrolling partners — $22.25 is Disney shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Experiences carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Experiences — parks, resorts and cruises — grew operating income 13% to $2,516M on 8% higher revenue, with domestic parks up 22% on higher attendance and guest spending. Sports profit rose 29% to $1,037M, helped by the absence of last year's $314M Star India loss.

takeaways.title: Streaming is now a real profit engine
takeaways.text: Entertainment operating income fell 15% to $1,022M as TV networks declined and last year's Inside Out 2 set an impossible comparison — but Direct-to-Consumer operating income swung to $346M from a $19M loss, with 183 million Disney+ and Hulu subscriptions.

takeaways.title: A tax benefit doubled the bottom line
takeaways.text: Reported net income was $5,943M ($2.92 a share), but $3.3B of it was a non-cash tax benefit recognized when Hulu's U.S. tax classification changed. Excluding such items, adjusted EPS was $1.61, up 16%.

oneTimers: A $3.3B non-cash tax benefit, recognized upon the change in Hulu's U.S. income tax classification, sits in the tax line (a $2,732M net tax benefit for the quarter) and accounts for most of the jump in reported net income.
Restructuring and impairment charges were $185M, primarily an impairment of an equity investment.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $324M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $75M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.
footerNote: Of the $5,943M of net income, $681M belongs to noncontrolling partners; $5,262M is attributable to Disney (the $2.92 EPS figure).
segmentNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $1,022M, Sports $1,037M, Experiences $2,516M (before corporate costs).
